scope: Independent offline pre-GPU audit of Gate B post-free ownership and refcount proof

resolved_findings.title: Detached KVCacheManager request-to-block tables could survive while Gate B reported PASS
resolved_findings.resolution: The proof now reads the exact vLLM 0.23 SingleTypeKVCacheManager.req_to_blocks key set through KVCacheManager.coordinator. Capture requires every declared source runtime ID in that native ownership map. Post-release requires every old runtime ID absent, exposes the result on the transaction proof and each block transition, and includes it in both passed predicates.

adversarial_rerun.error: v11 source release failed the post-free ownership gate

offline_validation.result: V11OwnershipProofError with both deliberately stale native tables still present

evidence: The boundary rejects adapter proxies by exact VllmLiveStateAdapter type and verifies the pinned vLLM 0.23.0 view.
Capture and release require a currently held EXPORT_CAPTURE witness bound to the exact scheduler and KV manager.

The pre-release proof cross-checks logical owners, runtime owners, native refcounts, exact physical block coverage, allocator-issued epochs, KV pool byte accounting, and native req_to_blocks membership.
Release invokes the adapter's real destroy_branch/destroy_session paths, which bind to LLMEngine.abort_request, KVCacheManager.free, and reset_prefix_cache.

The post-release proof checks native refcount zero, allocator availability, hash absence, allocator epoch tombstones, root-reference absence, scheduler referrer absence, exact native request-table absence, full free pool, and allocator-visible KV byte reclamation.

The expected_source_block_count and expected_allocation_epochs interfaces require exact count and identity coverage, so the production run must provide all 1152 source blocks rather than a sampled subset.
limitations: This is an offline structural and adversarial review; no A100 allocation was made.
The local fixture validates the count-generic per-block algorithm on three blocks. Exact 1152-block runtime records remain a mandatory output of the real-A100 micro-validation.
